title: The conversation backpack
objectives: Separate stored history from the messages sent to a model.
Explain why a context budget can omit an earlier fact.
prediction: Your app saves four messages but only sends the newest two. Can the model see an earlier name just because it is saved in the database?
explanation: Imagine a conversation backpack with limited space. Your app has a shelf containing all saved messages, but only the messages packed for this request are available through that request's conversation context.

A context window is a model-specific limit on tokenized request material, with output limits that also need planning. The app must choose which instructions, prior turns, notes, and current question fit. Stored history is not automatically the same as selected context.
Our Python toy keeps two recent messages using a list slice. A slice such as messages[-2:] returns the last two list items. It makes the selection visible, but counts messages rather than tokens.

If an earlier personal name is omitted and not supplied elsewhere, the model cannot use that stored message through this request. It might guess, so an application should not treat a lucky answer as proof that context selection worked. In the real app, preserve instructions, valid role ordering, and an output budget.
analogy_limit: A backpack is a selection analogy, not a model memory architecture. The last-two-message toy is not a production context policy. Real requests must account for tokens, roles, instructions, notes, and output reserve.

python_example.code:
messages = [
    {'role': 'user', 'text': 'My name is Mira.'},
    {'role': 'assistant', 'text': 'Hello Mira.'},
    {'role': 'user', 'text': 'I like puzzles.'},
    {'role': 'assistant', 'text': 'Let us try a puzzle.'},
]
selected = messages[-2:]
print('saved:', len(messages))
print('selected:', len(selected))
for message in selected:
    print(message['role'] + ': ' + message['text'])
python_example.expected_output:
saved: 4
selected: 2
user: I like puzzles.
assistant: Let us try a puzzle.
walkthrough: The slice creates the request's selected-history toy, without deleting the original list.
The name appears in the saved messages but not in selected.
A real current user question would be added after valid selected history; this example only inspects the selection.

game.title: Memory Backpack
game.instructions: Decide what the model can use from the packed context. Separate saved storage from request content. Get two of three right.

rounds.prompt: Four messages are saved, but selected contains only the last two. How many messages did our toy pack?

choices.text: Four
Two
All messages ever written

feedback.a: The slice selected two list entries.
feedback.b: Four were saved, but saving and selecting are different.
feedback.c: This code only uses the list shown and its slice.

rounds.prompt: The name Mira was in an omitted message. What does this reveal?

choices.text: The name is absent from this selected request context
The name was erased from the database
The model was retrained to forget

feedback.a: The original list remains; selection does not delete saved history.
feedback.b: The packed messages do not include that name.
feedback.c: Context selection does not retrain model parameters.

rounds.prompt: Which is the better future app policy?

choices.text: Keep valid roles/instructions and select history under a token budget
Always take two messages and call it exact token budgeting
Always send unlimited history

feedback.a: Models and apps have input/output limits.
feedback.b: Two messages may have very different token counts.
feedback.c: A real policy accounts for structure and size while preserving necessary context.

choices.text: Counts exact model tokens
Returns the last two items
Deletes the first two saved items

feedback.a: Negative indexes count backward from the end.
feedback.b: This slice returns a new list; it does not delete the original history.
feedback.c: It selects messages, not tokenizes them.

questions.prompt: What makes saved history useful to a stateless model request?

choices.text: The app including relevant saved content in the request
Changing a CSS color
Merely keeping a SQLite file on disk

feedback.a: The provider does not automatically read your local database.
feedback.b: The app chooses and supplies relevant context.
feedback.c: Presentation does not alter the request content.

questions.prompt: Which three mechanisms should stay distinct?

choices.text: Fonts, colors, and margins
Trained parameters, stored app history, and selected request context
Tea, juice, and water

feedback.a: Those are UI concerns, not the three model/app memory mechanisms.
feedback.c: They can affect behavior in different ways; saving is not training or automatic selection.

build.title: Inspect the backpack
build.instructions: Change the example to select the last three messages. Print which messages are selected and whether any contains Mira. Compare this to selecting only the last two. Keep the full saved list unchanged.
criteria: The three-message selection includes 'Hello Mira.' while the two-message selection does not.
The saved list still contains four messages after both selections.
hints: any('Mira' in m['text'] for m in selected) tests whether at least one selected message contains the name.
build.reference_solution:
With messages from the example:
for count in [3, 2]:
    selected = messages[-count:]
    print(count, any('Mira' in m['text'] for m in selected))
print('saved:', len(messages))
Expected: 3 True; 2 False; saved: 4.

reflection: Explain how your future chatbot will keep saved history separate from the messages sent to Google.
tutor_context: Explain list slices, saved history, selected context, and trained parameters. The backpack is a token-budget analogy; last-N messages is only a toy. Do not infer context correctness from a lucky model guess.

visual.title: Pack a smaller conversation backpack
visual.inputs: Four saved messages form two complete user/assistant pairs.
visual.operation: messages[-2:] makes a new list containing the last two messages.
visual.output: Four remain saved; only the puzzle pair is selected.
visual.limit: This exact slice is safe only for this alternating four-message toy. The real app selects bounded whole turns.

frames.title: Save two pairs
frames.explain: These rows are the app record. Saving them does not train a model.

frames.title: Select the tail
frames.explain: -2 means start two positions from the end. The earlier name pair stays saved but is omitted from selected.

frames.title: Count two different lists
frames.explain: len(messages) stays 4. len(selected) is 2. A slice does not erase the original list.

frames.title: Print the selected context
frames.explain: The loop visits only selected. The name Mira is absent from these two printed messages.

saved: 4
selected: 2
user: I like puzzles.
assistant: Let us try a puzzle.

challenge.question: After the slice, is Mira erased from the saved messages?

choices.text: Yes, slicing deletes the older entries
choices.feedback: A slice creates another list. The original messages still has four entries.

choices.text: No, it is saved but omitted from selected
choices.feedback: Correct. Saved history and selected context are different.
